svg.text: Entity Relationship Diagram — Event Registration System
10 tables · crow’s-foot notation · solid = enforced foreign key, dashed = nullable reference (audit trail and outbox)
dashed FK: user_id → USERS, event_id → EVENTS (both nullable)
purged on expiry · no foreign key
0..* = zero or many · 0..1 = optional one · dashed = nullable reference
Keys, constraints and rules enforced by the schema
Duplicate rule: UNIQUE (event_id, user_id) on REGISTRATIONS — one registration per participant per event.
Capacity rule: COUNT(status = 'confirmed') may never exceed EVENTS.max_participants; checked inside a transaction with a row lock.
Attendance rule: UNIQUE (registration_id) on ATTENDANCE — a participant can be checked in only once, and only while confirmed.
Venue rule: UNIQUE (name, city) on VENUES; EVENTS.venue_id is NOT NULL, so the venue name is stored once.
Referential integrity: REGISTRATIONS → USERS/EVENTS, ATTENDANCE → REGISTRATIONS, REGISTRATION_STATUS_CHANGES → REGISTRATIONS → ON DELETE CASCADE;
AUDIT_LOGS.actor_id and the audit columns use ON DELETE SET NULL so history survives a deleted user.
Soft delete: EVENTS.deleted_at keeps an archived event’s registrations, attendance and status history available for reports.
Indexes: USERS(email UQ, reset_password_token UQ, role), VENUES(name, city UQ), EVENTS(event_date, venue_id),
REGISTRATIONS(event_id,status), (user_id,status), (status,registration_date) — the FIFO waitlist queue; ATTENDANCE(registration_id UQ);
Outbox: NOTIFICATIONS is written in the same transaction as the change it describes, then drained by the worker and retried up to 3 times.
Guest access: MANAGE_TOKENS stores only the SHA-256 of the link token; USERS.password is NULL until the account is claimed (claimed_at), so a guest never needs a password to cancel.
SESSIONS: no foreign key — it stores the serialised express-session payload and is purged by expiry.
Normalisation: 1NF/2NF/3NF are satisfied for every table shown; the one remaining 3NF exception is the single-use reset token on USERS.
A stricter variant (PASSWORD_RESET_TOKENS, lookup tables, NOTIFICATIONS) is proposed in docs/schema-3nf.sql.
